rationale: The corrected multi-voter declaration executed cleanly. Receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 (exit 0, twenty events, no parse loss) resolves all four comparisons: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, the restarted leader of a five-voter cluster came back holding the snapshot's three-voter configuration at index 1 instead of the log's index 14 with five servers (comparison 0 violated, witness event index 15), while the flag-off control kept index 14 and five servers (comparison 2 holds, evaluated index 18). The election check behaved differently from the previous receipt: this time the isolated restarted node did not win (comparisons 1 and 3 both hold, evaluated indices 16 and 19), whereas receipt 63a30ed680b741199ddd7877237d5874 recorded the same node becoming leader with two of the three committed votes while the majority side kept its leader. Both observations are retained, no rate or absence claim is made, and a gap records that reproduction question. The configuration-loss claim for a real membership change is now witnessed, so the child question is marked violated for that comparison while the election consequence stays unresolved; the parent question's account is unchanged and still accurate for what it witnessed.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose latest snapshot predates committed membership changes resumes with the snapshot's configuration: after growing a three-voter cluster to five voters, the restarted leader held configuration index 1 with three servers while its own log's latest configuration was index 14 with five servers, and the same restart without the flag kept index 14 with five servers.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; one snapshot taken before the membership change (automatic snapshots disabled); the committed configuration entry's index at or below the persisted commit index restored by restoreFromCommittedLogs.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: Receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 (exit 0, twenty events, no parse loss) completes the corrected declaration. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 15: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, the node restarted from a log whose latest configuration is index 14 with five servers came back at configuration index 1 with three servers (the snapshot's bootstrap configuration), and comparison 2 holds for the flag-off control at evaluated event index 18 (index 14, five servers). That establishes the configuration loss for a real membership change, not just a bootstrap entry, and matches the same values seen in the earlier receipt. The election check did not reproduce: comparisons 1 and 3 hold at evaluated event indices 16 and 19, meaning the isolated restarted node did not become leader in this execution, whereas receipt 63a30ed680b741199ddd7877237d5874 recorded the same node becoming leader with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3 while majority_side_leader was true. Both observations are kept: one occurrence and one non-occurrence under the same declaration, so neither a rate nor an absence is claimed, and the reproduction question is registered as a gap with an exploratory successor. Source reading explains why the consequence is possible at all: with the stale three-server list quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) returns two and electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) counts only that list, so the node's own vote plus one follower meets the stale quorum while the committed five-voter configuration needs three. The configuration loss itself follows the parent mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advances lastApplied past the committed configuration before the scan at api.go:604-620, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is not re-read.
counterevidence: The flag-off control keeps index 14 with five servers through the same membership change and restart, isolating the recovery path.

The minority-leadership consequence did not appear in this execution's comparison 1 (event 16: became_leader false), so the safety consequence beyond the lost configuration remains unresolved rather than asserted.
limitations: The membership change exercised is an addition of voters, and the restarted node was the leader; other roles and change types are not witnessed.
The election consequence is recorded as one occurrence and one non-occurrence; no occurrence-rate or absence bound is claimed.
No entry-level divergence between the two leaders after a minority election is observed.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts executed the same harness file and scenario (three-voter bootstrap, one deliberate snapshot before the change, growth to five voters, restart of the leading node from identical stores). Receipt 63a30ed680b741199ddd7877237d5874 carried the same configuration values (index 1 with three servers against expected 14 with five, control 14 with five) and additionally showed the isolated node winning; receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 is the corrected declaration over the same inputs and shows the same configuration values but no minority win. They are separate complete executions rather than fragments of one history, and the differing election observation is recorded as schedule sensitivity, not merged.

scope.description: Exploratory follow-up on the reproduction of the minority-leadership consequence: the same five-voter scenario as the completed multi-voter experiment, with the isolation applied immediately after the restart instead of after the majority side has settled, and with the observation window extended, to see whether the restarted node's campaign reaches leadership with two votes while the majority side keeps its own leader.
assumptions: The restarted node's stale three-voter configuration gives it a quorum of two while the committed five-voter configuration requires three.
Isolating it before it re-learns the majority leader removes the 'reject votes while a leader exists' protection from the single partner it keeps.
excluded: Any occurrence-rate or absence claim; a single run cannot bound the frequency.
Entry-level divergence after a minority leadership, which needs a separate setup.

experiment.prefix: The harness reuses the same facilities as the completed multi-voter experiment (MakeClusterCustom with Peers 3, CommitTrackingLogs, RestoreCommittedLogs; one deliberate Snapshot; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(2) merged and two AddVoter calls; ten further Apply calls; Shutdown and NewRaft on the same stores with a fresh inmem transport), but partitions the restarted node together with one committed voter as soon as the restart returns, before the majority side settles, and samples both sides for a longer bounded window. It emits multivoter_after_restart and multivoter_partition_election events carrying the same operands, plus the term and last log index of the restarted node and its partner, and no production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns the quorum arithmetic a restarted node applies; if the rebuilt configuration is stale, the election it can win is a decision the committed configuration would refuse.

comparisons.description: With isolation applied immediately after the restart, an election on the isolated side must still not produce a leader whose support is below the committed configuration's quorum; the defect prediction is that it does.
